h1: The 5 Best 1000VA UPS Battery Backups for PCs and Desks, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best 1000VA UPS Battery Backups: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 UPS battery backups at or near 1000VA scored on real watts, waveform, AVR, runtime visibility and value for PCs and networks.
summary: The GOLDENMATE 1000VA/800W lithium UPS is the pick for buyers who want the most usable wattage, because it delivers 800 watts from the same 1000VA label that others cap near 600. The CyberPower CP1000PFCLCD is the safest choice for an active PFC power supply thanks to pure sine wave output, the APC BX1000M is the standard office desktop answer, and the CyberPower CP1000AVRLCD adds an informative LCD at a familiar price.
intro: The number on the box is the least useful figure on a UPS. VA is an apparent power rating, and the number that decides whether your computer survives is watts, which on most 1000VA units sits between 500 and 800. Buyers who match their PC to the VA figure and ignore the wattage are the ones who find the unit beeping in overload the first time a graphics card spins up.

This ranking therefore sorts by usable watts, output waveform, voltage regulation and what the unit tells you while it runs. We reviewed five backups from their listings and spec sheets: four sold at 1000VA and one 850VA model that competes for the same buyer at a lower cost. Each was scored on how well it protects a desktop, a modem and a router, not on how impressive the VA number looks.

products.name: GOLDENMATE 1000VA/800W Lithium UPS Battery Backup & Surge Protector, White
products.verdict: The most real wattage at the 1000VA tier, in a compact lithium-battery case.
products.description:
The GOLDENMATE is rated 1000VA and 800W and uses a lithium battery, with surge protection and a compact footprint. A gray version of the same unit is also sold. The 800W figure is the headline: it is well above the watts-to-VA ratio of the traditional lead-acid models in this group.

It takes the top spot because more watts at the same capacity tier means less risk of overload for a gaming or workstation PC, and lithium cells typically last longer than sealed lead-acid ones and weigh less. Against the CyberPower PFC below, it gives up what the listing does not promise, which is pure sine wave output, so check the product page for the waveform before connecting an active PFC power supply.

Buy it if your PC draws more than a basic office machine and you want headroom. Be mindful that a newer product line has a shorter public track record than APC or CyberPower, so read the warranty terms.
products.idealFor: Gaming and workstation PCs that need real watt headroom.
products.skipIf: You must have confirmed pure sine wave output.

products.name: CyberPower CP1000PFCLCD PFC Sinewave UPS Battery Backup and Surge Protector
products.verdict: Pure sine wave output with AVR and an LCD, aimed at PCs with active PFC power supplies.
products.description:
The CP1000PFCLCD is a 1000VA-class unit with a PFC sinewave output, automatic voltage regulation and an LCD readout. It is listed as compatible with APFC power supplies, which is the reason this model exists.

It ranks second because waveform is the one spec that can actually cause trouble. Many cheaper backups produce a stepped, simulated sine wave on battery, and some active PFC power supplies in modern PCs can shut down or misbehave when fed that shape. A pure sine unit removes the question. It sits below the GOLDENMATE because the listing does not trumpet a higher wattage, and lead-acid runtime is limited.

Choose it for a modern desktop with an APFC supply, and for anyone who wants to remove waveform risk. The caveat is cost: sine wave models carry a premium over the AVR-only units in this ranking.
pros: LCD shows status at a glance
cons: Real watts not highlighted in listing
products.idealFor: Modern PCs with an active PFC power supply.
products.skipIf: You only protect a modem and a router.

products.name: APC 1000VA/600W Pro UPS Battery Backup for Office Electronics, AVR, BX1000M
products.verdict: The standard, well-proven 1000VA pick for a basic office desktop.
products.description:
The APC BX1000M is rated 1000VA and 600W, with AVR, multiple outlets and a listing that targets office electronics. It is the unit most IT buyers would name first, and it is the benchmark in the 1000VA class.

It lands third because the 600W figure is lower than the GOLDENMATE and the unit has no waveform claim to match the PFC model. What you get in return is an established platform with easy-to-find replacement batteries and a familiar warranty path. For a typical desktop, monitor and router, 600 watts is plenty.

Buy it for an office PC that does not draw heavy GPU load. Skip it if you run a gaming rig or workstation that spikes above the 600W ceiling, and verify that your power supply works with a simulated sine wave.
pros: Replacement batteries are easy to find
cons: No sine wave claim in listing
products.idealFor: Office desktops, monitors and network gear.
products.skipIf: Your PC draws heavy GPU load.

products.name: CyberPower CP1000AVRLCD Intelligent LCD UPS Battery Backup
products.verdict: A familiar CyberPower design with AVR, surge protection and a load-aware LCD.
products.description:
The CP1000AVRLCD is a 1000VA-class unit with AVR, surge protection and an intelligent LCD that reports load and status. It is an established design in the CyberPower line, and it covers the usual desktop-and-router job.

It ranks fourth because it matches the APC on most counts and the LCD is its distinguishing feature. Seeing load and estimated runtime matters more than people expect, since it tells you whether the next monitor or printer will push the unit past its limit. It sits below the PFC model because the listing makes no sine wave claim, and below the APC for the plainer reason that the APC has a broader reputation in offices.

Pick it if you want visibility into load and runtime at a typical 1000VA price. If your PC uses an active PFC supply, spend a little more on the PFC variant.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want visible load and runtime data.
products.skipIf: You own a PC with an APFC power supply.

products.name: APC 850VA/510W Pro UPS Battery Backup for Office Electronics, AVR, BX850M
products.verdict: A smaller 850VA/510W APC for buyers who want near-1000VA protection and a lower bill.
products.description:
The BX850M is the smaller sibling at 850VA and 510W, with AVR and a compact form factor. It is not a 1000VA unit, and it is included because the buyers who shop at this tier often compare it against the BX1000M to save money.

It finishes fifth because 510W is the lowest usable power in the ranking, and the gap from the BX1000M is narrower than the price difference may suggest. It makes sense for a modest PC, a monitor and a router, where the load stays well below 400 watts and the extra capacity of the larger unit would sit unused.

Buy it if you have a low-draw setup and want APC reliability for less. Skip it if you plan to add a second monitor, a printer or a more powerful graphics card, since you will outgrow the 510W ceiling quickly.
pros: APC platform at a lower cost
products.idealFor: Light desktop setups with modest power draw.
products.skipIf: You expect to add hardware later.

methodology.title: Usable wattage
methodology.description: We compared the watt rating, not the VA label, because watts decide whether a UPS can carry the load without alarms or shutdowns.

methodology.title: Output waveform
methodology.description: Pure sine wave output and APFC compatibility score higher, since a stepped waveform can cause trouble for modern power supplies on battery.

methodology.title: Voltage regulation
methodology.description: Automatic voltage regulation corrects brownouts without draining the battery, so we favored units that include AVR.

methodology.title: Monitoring and outlets
methodology.description: An LCD with load and runtime data, plus enough surge and battery outlets for a desk, make a unit easier to live with.

methodology.title: Battery life and support
methodology.description: We weighed battery chemistry, how easy replacements are to buy, and the reputation of the platform behind the unit.

whatMatters.detail: VA is apparent power, and watts is real power, so a 1000VA unit with a 600W rating can carry less than one rated 800W. This matters because your PC's power supply label and your actual draw are in watts. Add up your computer, monitor and network gear, and make sure the total stays under about 80 percent of the unit's watt rating.

On battery, cheap UPS units output a stepped approximation of a sine wave, while better ones output a true sine wave. Many power supplies tolerate the stepped version, but some active PFC models can shut off or buzz. Check your power supply's manual and look for PFC sinewave or pure sine wave in the listing.

Automatic voltage regulation boosts or trims the incoming voltage during brownouts and surges without switching to the battery. It matters if your area has frequent dips, because every battery transfer shortens cell life. Look for AVR on the listing and treat it as a standard feature at this price.

Lead-acid batteries are cheap and replaceable but heavy and short-lived, usually needing replacement after a few years. Lithium units are lighter and tend to last longer. Runtime at 1000VA is typically minutes for a loaded PC, so plan on enough time to save work and shut down, not to keep working.

An LCD that shows load, input voltage and estimated runtime turns guesswork into numbers. Outlets split into battery-backed and surge-only, and you want enough battery ones for the PC, monitor and modem. Check the outlet count and which ones are backed before you buy.

cards.label: Pure sine
cards.text: Output matches wall power on battery, which is the safe choice for active PFC power supplies and sensitive audio gear. The CyberPower CP1000PFCLCD is the pick in this ranking built around that feature.

cards.label: Simulated sine
cards.text: A stepped waveform costs less and works with most power supplies and with routers and modems. The APC BX1000M and the CyberPower CP1000AVRLCD fit here, and they are fine for a typical office PC.

faq.q: Is a 1000VA UPS compatible with my PC?
faq.a: It depends on watts. Add up the real draw of your PC, monitor and network gear and keep it below about 80 percent of the unit's watt rating, which ranges from 510W to 800W here. Check your power supply for APFC and choose a pure sine wave model if it has one.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying a UPS?
faq.a: Buying on the VA number alone. Two units with the same VA can differ by a couple of hundred watts, and the weaker one will overload under a gaming load. Read the watt rating on the listing and size to that.

faq.q: Is a pure sine wave UPS worth it over a simulated one?
faq.a: If your PC has an active PFC power supply, yes, because a stepped waveform can cause shutdowns or noise on battery. For a modem, router or basic office PC, a simulated sine wave unit is usually fine and costs less.

faq.q: How do I set up a UPS correctly?
faq.a: Plug the UPS directly into a wall outlet, never into a power strip, and put the PC, monitor and modem on the battery-backed outlets. Printers and chargers belong on surge-only outlets. Install the monitoring software if the unit offers a USB connection so the PC shuts down on its own.

faq.q: How often do UPS batteries need replacing?
faq.a: Lead-acid batteries in the APC and CyberPower units usually need replacing every three to five years, and heat shortens that. Lithium units last longer but are not user-replaceable in the same way. Run a self-test every few months and replace the battery when runtime drops noticeably.

faq.q: Can I plug a laser printer into a UPS?
faq.a: Avoid it. Laser printers draw a large surge while warming up and can overload a 1000VA unit even when the average draw seems low. Plug the printer into a surge-only outlet or a separate protector.

finalTake: Buy the GOLDENMATE if you want the most real wattage, and buy the CyberPower CP1000PFCLCD if your PC has an active PFC supply and you want clean sine wave power on battery. The APC BX1000M remains the dependable choice for a normal office desktop, and the CyberPower CP1000AVRLCD adds useful load data. Take the APC BX850M only if your load is genuinely small, and always size the unit by watts rather than VA.
